root_cause.text: Incorrect ordering of devm-managed resource allocations in the pm8916_lbc charger driver, where the IRQ handler is registered before the power_supply device, causing a use-after-free when the handler accesses the freed power_supply during device removal (and potential use of uninitialized pointer during probe).
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states that requesting IRQ before registering the power_supply via devm leads to the power_supply being deallocated before the IRQ handler is freed, creating a race where an interrupt can call power_supply_changed() on a freed handle. The patch diff confirms the fix by moving devm_request_threaded_irq() to after the power_supply registration.

    power: supply: Add driver for pm8916 lbc
    
    pm8916 LBC is a Linear Battery Charger hardware block in pm8916 PMIC.
    
    This block implements simple CC/CV charging for Li-Po batteries.
    The hardware has internal state machine to switch between modes and
    works mostly autonomously, only needing the limits and targets to be
    set to operate.
bic_trace_step.reason: In the probe function, devm_request_threaded_irq is called at line ~260 before devm_power_supply_register at line ~330. The IRQ handler pm8916_lbc_charger_state_changed_irq accesses chg->charger (via power_supply_changed(chg->charger)) which is NULL until registered. Additionally, during removal devm resources are freed in reverse order, so power_supply will be freed before the IRQ, causing a use-after-free when the handler runs. No NULL check or reordering is present.
